title: Corso di Italiano — Livello A0
shortDescription: The SS Europa classroom course, chapter by chapter: start from zero with the same lessons, slides and tests as your teacher. With English and Punjabi.
description:
This is the official SS Europa Italian course used in our classes, for complete beginners from India, Pakistan and Bangladesh who are going to Italy to work, study or live.

Each chapter (Capitolo) follows the lessons of the classroom: every 60-minute class is split into three short lessons you can study on your phone, with pictures, audio, grammar tables and exercises. Every word comes with its English and Punjabi meaning, and the slides of each class are attached as PDF. Each chapter ends with a test (pass mark 60%); the written part and the oral interview are done with your teacher.
objectives:
Read and pronounce Italian correctly: the alphabet, C and G, the final accents
Greet people and introduce yourself: name, city, nationality, age and phone number
Understand the teacher and name the objects of the classroom
Fill in a form with your personal details, dates and numbers up to 100
Talk about your family and describe people
Use essere and avere, the articles, plurals, possessives and adjectives

lessons.title: Lesson 1 · The Italian alphabet
lessons.summary: The 21 Italian letters, how to say them and one word for each letter.

blocks.title: Class slides: Capitolo 1 · Lezione 1 (PDF)
blocks.body: The slides your teacher uses in class. Open them on your phone or print them.

blocks.title: Le 21 lettere italiane
blocks.body:
The Italian alphabet has **21 letters**: A B C D E F G H I L M N O P Q R S T U V Z.

The letters **J, K, W, X, Y** are "foreign letters" (lettere straniere). They are used only in foreign words such as *jeans*, *kiwi*, *web*, *taxi*, *yoga*.

The 5 vowels (vocali) are **A, E, I, O, U**. In Italian every vowel is always pronounced, and always in the same way.

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: A vowel with an accent at the end of a word (**città, caffè, sì, però, più**) is said **strong and clear**, with the voice on the last syllable. The accent can change the meaning: **si** (oneself) / **sì** (yes).

lessons.title: Lesson 1 · Pronunciation: C and G
lessons.summary: Soft and hard C and G: ciao or casa? gelato or gatto?

blocks.title: La lettera C: suono dolce e suono duro
blocks.body:
**C** has two sounds:

- **Soft [ch]** like *church* (Punjabi "ch", chachā) before **E** and **I**: **ce, ci** — and **cia, cio, ciu**.
- **Hard [k]** like *cat* (Punjabi "k", kakkā) before **A, O, U**: **ca, co, cu** — and **che, chi** (the H makes it hard).

blocks.title: La lettera G: suono dolce e suono duro
blocks.body:
**G** works the same way:

- **Soft [j]** like *gel* (Punjabi "j", jajjā): **ge, gi** — and **gia, gio, giu**.
- **Hard [g]** like *go* (Punjabi "g", gaggā): **ga, go, gu** — and **ghe, ghi**.

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: Remember the trick: **H after C or G makes the sound hard** (chiave, spaghetti). **I after C or G makes it soft** (ciao, giorno) and the I is almost not heard.

lessons.title: Lesson 3 · How old are you? The verb "avere"
lessons.titleIt: Lezione 3 · Quanti anni hai? Il verbo avere
lessons.summary: Io ho, tu hai, lui/lei ha — and how Italians say their age.

blocks.title: Il verbo AVERE (to have · H muta!)

blocks.body:
The **H** of *ho, hai, ha* is silent (muta): **ho** sounds like "o", **ha** like "a".

In Italian you **have** years: *Ho 20 anni* = I am 20 (literally "I have 20 years"). Punjabi: *Merī umar 20 sāl hai*.

items.punjabi: Āp jī dī umar kinnī hai?

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: Never say "Sono 20 anni" — that is wrong. Use **avere**: **Ho 20 anni.**

lessons.title: Lesson 4 · Masculine, feminine and un / uno / una / un'
lessons.titleIt: Lezione 4 · Maschile, femminile e articoli indeterminativi
lessons.summary: Nouns in -o and -a, and how to say "a / an" in Italian.

blocks.title: Maschile (-O) e femminile (-A)
blocks.body:
Every Italian noun is **masculine** or **feminine**.

- **Masculine** nouns usually end in **-O**: libro, quaderno, tavolo (Pulling: akkhar -O nāl khatam hundā hai)
- **Feminine** nouns usually end in **-A**: penna, sedia, lavagna (Istrīling: akkhar -A nāl khatam hundā hai)

blocks.title: Articoli indeterminativi (a / an · Ikk)
table: un libro · un tavolo · un banco

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: **Un'** with the apostrophe is only for **feminine** words that start with a vowel (un'aula). Masculine words with a vowel take **un** without apostrophe: *un amico, un orologio*.

blocks.body: The form in **-a / -i** (ascolta, leggi) is for **one** student. The form in **-ate / -ete** (ascoltate, leggete) is for the **whole class**.

blocks.title: Test Capitolo 1
blocks.body:
This test checks everything in Chapter 1: alphabet and pronunciation, greetings, introducing yourself (essere / avere), numbers 0–20 and classroom objects.

- **1. Listening** — listen and choose the word or number
- **2. Vocabulary and greetings**
- **3. Grammar** — essere, avere and un / uno / una / un'
- **4. Writing** — build sentences to introduce yourself

You need **60%** to pass. You can repeat the test as many times as you like.

lessons.title: Lesson 3 · Possessives: mio, tuo, suo…
lessons.summary: My, your, his, her, our, their — and the golden rule for family words.

blocks.title: Regola d'oro: possessivi e famiglia
blocks.body:
**Singular family word → NO article**
- mio padre (NO "il mio padre")
- tua madre (NO "la tua madre")
- suo fratello · nostra sorella

**Plural, and with LORO → WITH the article**
- i miei fratelli · le mie sorelle
- i nostri genitori
- il loro padre · la loro madre

items.punjabi: Mere pitā dā nām Gurdev hai.

items.italian: Le mie sorelle vivono in India.
items.punjabi: Merīāṁ bhaiṇāṁ India vich rahindīāṁ han.
Uhnāṁ dā puttar 5 sāl dā hai.

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: **Suo / sua** means both *his* and *her*: it agrees with the thing owned, not with the owner. *Marco e sua sorella* (Marco and his sister) · *Anna e suo fratello* (Anna and her brother).

options.text: I nostri genitori sono in India.

blocks.title: The situation
blocks.body: Two classmates talk about their families during the break.

lines.speaker: A
lines.italian: Hai fratelli o sorelle, Navdeep?
lines.english: Do you have brothers or sisters, Navdeep?
lines.punjabi: Kī tuhāḍe bharā jāṁ bhaiṇāṁ han?

lines.speaker: Navdeep
lines.italian: Sì! Ho un fratello e due sorelle.
lines.english: Yes! I have one brother and two sisters.
lines.punjabi: Hāṁ, merā ikk bharā ate do bhaiṇāṁ han.

lines.speaker: A

lines.english: My brother is tall and very nice. He lives in Mantova!
lines.punjabi: Merā bharā lambā ate bahut milansār hai. Uh Mantova vich rahindā hai!

blocks.title: Attività: parla della famiglia
blocks.body:
1. **Sei sposato/a o celibe/nubile?** — Are you married or single? (Kī tusīṁ viāhe ho?)
2. **Hai figli, fratelli o sorelle?** — Do you have children or siblings?
3. **Come si chiama tuo padre / tua madre?** — What is your father's / mother's name?

lessons.title: Lesson 4 · Noun–adjective agreement
lessons.summary: Adjectives with 4 forms (-o, -a, -i, -e) and with 2 forms (-e, -i).

blocks.title: Aggettivi a 2 forme (-E → -I)
table: mio fratello / mia sorella è giovane
i miei fratelli / le mie sorelle sono giovani
il signore / la signora è gentile
i signori / le signore sono gentili

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: The adjective takes the **gender and number** of the noun: la ragazza alt**a**, i ragazzi alt**i**. Adjectives in **-e** have only two forms: *gentile → gentili*.

blocks.title: Intervista il tuo compagno (interview your partner)
blocks.body:
1. **Chi è il tuo migliore amico / la tua migliore amica?** — Si chiama…
2. **Com'è?** (alto/basso, giovane/anziano, simpatico, gentile…) — È alto/a, giovane e molto simpatico/a!
3. **Quanti anni ha? Quanti fratelli o sorelle ha?** — Ha … anni e ha … fratelli / … sorelle.

lessons.summary: Listening, documents, calendar, family, articles, plurals, essere / avere, possessives and adjectives. Pass mark: 60%.

blocks.title: Test Capitolo 2
blocks.body:
This test checks everything in Chapter 2 (Lessons 1–4).

- **1. Listening** — days, months, documents, family, adjectives and numbers 21–100
- **2. Vocabulary** — documents, calendar, family and adjectives
- **3. Grammar** — articles and plurals, essere / avere, possessives, agreement and questions
- **4. Writing** — sentences about your family

You need **60%** to pass. You can repeat the test as many times as you like.
